rounds.report:
# video19 reconstruction report (L1 / Proxy, CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline)

Submitted scene: round 004 render (4 rendered rounds, 3 revisions after the initial scene).

Observed from the 24 reference samples:
- Four shots with hard cuts. A (t 0 to ~2.35 s): telephoto over-the-shoulder view behind a black mirrorless camera on a tripod (left foreground). The operator's hand presses the back buttons, the LCD menu highlight moves Interval -> Choose start -> Start, and the screen turns off at ~1.9 s. The mannequin head sits on a white turntable at right, in front of a white backdrop. B (~2.35 to ~3.65 s): wider view from the same side. The operator's dark-sleeved arm reaches in from the left/upper-left, grips the back/top-left of the camera, then withdraws. C (~3.65 to ~4.9 s): low frontal close-up of the head on the two-tier turntable. The turntable starts rotating at ~4.0 s and the face turns toward image-right. D (~4.9 to 5.84 s): frontal medium-wide shot with a letterbox bar at the top, and the head keeps turning to image-right (~33 to 47 deg yaw). A light stand is at right and an LED bar sits above the backdrop.
- The lower-third graphics ("REMOTE CONTROL" red outline frame; "Ecommerce" black box with white border, fading in at ~4.75 s) are post-production overlays. They are reproduced only as untextured camera-attached rectangles, with the text omitted at L1. The shot-D top letterbox bar is reproduced.

Geometry: boxes, cylinders and spheres for the table, the unlit white backdrop, the walls and floor, the light stand with its boom and two LED bars, the two-tier turntable (static base with groove and control button, rotating platter), the mannequin (bust, neck, cranium, jaw block, ears), the camera (body, grip, viewfinder hump, lens, hinged tilted LCD with menu highlight bars, ball head and column) and the operator (torso, head, shoulder, upper arm, forearm, palm, finger, thumb). The arm is posed by analytic two-bone IK from keyed wrist and fingertip targets.
Camera: four static per-shot perspective cameras with hard cuts at frames ~57, ~88 and ~118. Each cut frame is inferred between adjacent samples. Estimated vertical FOVs: A ~9 deg, B ~13 deg, C ~26 deg, D ~19 deg.
Timing: the head and platter yaw is 0 until ~4.0 s, then rises piecewise-linearly to ~47 deg at the end. Menu highlight changes at ~0.40 and 0.64 s, screen off at 1.88 s, small finger presses, arm reach keyframes 2.3 to 3.7 s.

Feedback and revisions: round 001 matched framing in A, C and D, but the shot-B arm path was wrong and the backdrop was grey. Round 002 brightened the backdrop (not tone-mapped), re-keyed the shot-B reach and resized the camera parts. Round 003 moved the shot-D camera farther back with a narrower FOV, which fixed the backdrop-to-turntable proportions, and enlarged the lens. Round 004 made small backdrop, LED-bar and jaw-proxy adjustments.

Remaining discrepancies and uncertainty: the backdrop extent cannot match exactly in every shot at once (it is slightly too wide in C and slightly misplaced in B). The hand and arm are blocky proxies with no motion blur, and the blurred foreground mass of the operator's head and shoulder in shot B is only partly represented. The mannequin proxy has no facial features, so its orientation reads mainly from the jaw block and ears. Overlay text is not reproduced. Lighting and tone are flatter than the reference. Exact cut frames, intermediate arm motion, world scale and the overlay animation curves are inferred, not observed.
